description:
About the Position

Amsterdam UMC advertises a doctoral (promovendus) position on international research into MLC, a rare hereditary disease of the brain white matter (megalencephalic leukoencephalopathy with subcortical cysts). The candidate joins the Amsterdam Leukodystrophy Centre's international research programme, which coordinates natural-history studies, biomarker development and therapy research with partner centres worldwide. The employment is a salaried four-year PhD position under the Dutch CAO-NU collective agreement, with a starting salary of EUR 3,217 per month.

The project combines clinical research on an international patient cohort with laboratory and imaging work aimed at understanding disease mechanisms and preparing treatment trials. The doctoral candidate works in a specialised team spanning neurology, genetics and imaging, and benefits from Amsterdam UMC's rare-disease infrastructure, patient registries and European collaborator network. Because parts of the research run in Dutch clinical settings, Dutch language skills are expected for patient-facing components.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in biomedical sciences, medicine, neuroscience or a related field, with interest in rare disease research and clinical translation. Experience with patient data, imaging analysis or cell models is an advantage. Applications are submitted through the Amsterdam UMC vacancy page, and the closing date for applications is 4 November 2026.

Highlights

  • PhD on MLC leukodystrophy within an international programme
  • Amsterdam Leukodystrophy Centre specialised environment
  • Natural-history, biomarker and therapy-preparation research
  • Salaried four-year position (EUR 3,217 - 4,077 per month)
  • European rare-disease collaborator network
  • Closing date: 4 November 2026

About Amsterdam UMC

Amsterdam UMC is the combined academic medical centre of the University of Amsterdam and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, operating from AMC and VUmc campuses. It is one of the largest biomedical research institutions in the Netherlands, with research programmes spanning infectious diseases, oncology, cardiovascular science, epidemiology, public health and health data science. The centre employs PhD candidates and postdocs on salaried contracts under the CAO-UMC collective agreement. Research vacancies are published on the werkenbij.amsterdamumc.org portal, and many doctoral projects are embedded in national and European research consortia.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official page before the deadline: 4 November 2026. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents - early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.
